sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Mount Prospect, Illinois?
sections.html:
Mount Prospect is a Cook County village, so a sale here can carry transfer charges at three levels: state, county and village. Plan for the village stamp step early, since it is separate from the county recording.

The village sits about 20 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and roughly 4 miles north of O'Hare Airport, partly in Elk Grove Township and partly in Wheeling Township. The Metra station and the closeness to O'Hare are the location points most listings lead with.

Most sellers choose among listing with an agent, selling directly to an investor or cash buyer, or trying a sale by owner. This page gives the village-specific facts for each.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Mount Prospect homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census counted 56,852 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 55,395, which is 2.6 percent below the 2020 estimates base. The village covers 10.72 square miles of land, about 5,304 people per square mile.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census reports a median owner-occupied value of $397,400 and a median gross rent of $1,502. Median monthly owner costs run $2,619 with a mortgage and $1,046 without one. Owners occupy 68.7 percent of housing units, and the village has 21,600 households at 2.56 people each. Median household income is $101,720.

The population profile is varied. The Census puts the foreign-born share at 29.6 percent, and 43.1 percent of residents age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home, so listing information in more than one language can widen your buyer pool. Almost half of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree or higher, at 48.6 percent.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Mount Prospect houses?
sections.html:
Several elementary districts divide the village, and the district for your address often matters more to buyers than the village name. Confirm it before you advertise.

  • Central Mount Prospect: Mount Prospect School District 57.
  • North and somewhat east: River Trails School District 26.
  • South and somewhat west: Elk Grove Community Consolidated School District 59.
  • Small northern, north central and northwest pockets: Buffalo Grove-Wheeling CCSD 21, Arlington Heights District 25 and Prospect Heights District 23.

Township High School District 214 covers the whole village. Prospect High School is the only district 214 high school inside Mount Prospect, and some students attend Elk Grove High School or Buffalo Grove High School. Park services also vary by address, with the Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Prospect Heights and River Trails park districts all serving parts of the village.

sections.h2: How do transit, jobs and shopping help a Mount Prospect sale?
sections.html:
The Mount Prospect Metra station is on the Union Pacific Northwest Line, with trains southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago and northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses fill in around the village.

Employment is local too. The village's 2025 financial report lists CVS Caremark and Robert Bosch Tool Corporation as its largest employers, followed by the Village, Mount Prospect School District 57, Township High School District 214, Rauland-Borg, Costco, Walmart, School District 59 and TJX. Randhurst Village is the best-known retail address, and companies based in the village include Cummins Allison, NTN USA and Rauland-Borg.

The village is fully urban, and the Köppen climate is humid continental, with hot humid summers and cold snowy winters, in hardiness zone 5b. Buyers will inspect roofs, sump pumps and furnaces for that reason.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes apply when a Mount Prospect house sells?
sections.html:
Three layers can apply. The Cook County Clerk's transfer fee page lists the State of Illinois at 50 cents per $500 and Cook County at 25 cents per $500, with the seller named as the liable party for both. Illinois law at 35 ILCS 200/31-15 sets the state rate the same way.

The village adds its own real estate transfer tax, collected through a transfer stamp. The Finance Department's Taxes and Service Fees page offers an online transfer stamp application, in-person stamps by appointment, a rebate form, and an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transactions such as removing a person from a deed. Ask Finance for the current village rate and who owes it, because it depends on the Village Code.

Cook County also lists a separate transfer fee for each municipality through the Clerk's search tool, so you can compare the village against its neighbors before a closing. Line these charges up in your net sheet early.

sections.h2: How are Mount Prospect property taxes billed?
sections.html:
The Cook County Treasurer bills property tax in two installments. The Treasurer's posted schedule shows the first installment for tax year 2025 was due April 1, 2026 and the second was due October 1, 2026, so both of those dates have passed. Earlier years ran on different dates, and Cook County posts the schedule for each year.

At a closing, the title company usually prorates the tax between buyer and seller using the most recent bill. Bring a copy of your latest bill and your parcel number. The Treasurer's site also lists exemptions, including the homeowner, senior, senior freeze, disability and disabled veteran exemptions, so a buyer who qualifies can ask about them after the sale.

The village has also run a property tax relief grant for qualifying single-family owners, described on the same Finance page as a rebate of part of the village portion of the Cook County bill. Ask Finance whether the program is open before you count on it.

sections.h2: What building rules and disclosures apply before you sell?
sections.html:
Illinois requires a seller of residential property to complete the statutory disclosure report and deliver it before the contract is signed, under 765 ILCS 77/20. In Mount Prospect, buyers also look for permit history on roofs, additions, finished basements and mechanical work.

The village keeps its Village Code online through its code library, and its Community Development Department is the place to ask about permits, inspections and code questions. If the house is a rental, ask the village what license or inspection applies to your address before you list.

  • Request permit records for work done during your ownership.
  • Resolve open code notices, since an unresolved notice can complicate the closing.
  • Confirm the water, sewer and refuse account status with the village before closing.

If the house has ever had water in the basement, disclose it on the report and keep any repair invoices ready.

sections.h2: How do the three ways to sell compare in Mount Prospect?
sections.html:
A list-and-wait sale gives you the broadest exposure but adds showings, an inspection and the buyer's mortgage timeline. In a village where median household income is $101,720, an updated house in a sought-after school zone may draw more than one offer.

  • Agent listing: best when the house shows well and you can wait for a conventional closing.
  • For sale by owner: saves the listing fee but puts the disclosure form, contract and stamp paperwork on you.
  • Direct sale to a cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often pick, with an offer adjusted for repairs.

Whatever you choose, request the offer in writing, ask who pays each transfer charge, and keep the village stamp on your checklist.

faqs.q: Does Mount Prospect have its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The village issues real estate transfer stamps through its Finance Department, which offers an online application and in-person stamps by appointment. Ask Finance for the current rate and who owes it, since the village sets it separately from the state and county charges.

faqs.q: How much is the Cook County transfer fee?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk lists the county fee as 25 cents per $500, with the seller as the liable party, alongside the State of Illinois fee of 50 cents per $500.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Mount Prospect house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Central areas are in District 57, north and east areas in River Trails District 26, south and west areas in District 59, and small northern pockets in Districts 21, 25 and 23. Township High School District 214 covers the whole village.

faqs.q: What if I need to remove someone from a Mount Prospect deed?
faqs.a: The village Finance page links an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transactions, such as removing an individual from a deed. Use it with the deed and the transfer declaration, and ask Finance whether your case qualifies.

faqs.q: When are Cook County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For tax year 2025, the first installment was due April 1, 2026 and the second October 1, 2026. Due dates differ from year to year, so check the Cook County Treasurer's due dates page for the bill you hold.
